mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a supply-driven inflation scare that will pressure the Fed to tighten policy and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE does not rise
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, indicating the market is discounting a 'soft landing' rather than a hard tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in payroll employment, if accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate, signals a cyclical labor market turning point that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy enters a recession.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE also rises
failure_condition: Leading economic indicators (e.g., yield curve, consumer confidence) do not confirm an imminent recession within the next 6 months, negating the bearish signal.

mechanism_narrative: A collapse in housing starts, if not offset by a rise in retail sales, signals a demand-driven growth scare that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in a potential recession.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% in 1 month and RSAFS does not rise
failure_condition: The housing starts decline is subsequently reversed in the following month, indicating the initial drop was a temporary blip rather than the start of a sustained downtrend.

mechanism_narrative: A surprise interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, not already priced into the market, will produce an immediate negative S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days as the market adjusts to the new policy stance.
failure_condition: The rate hike is accompanied by dovish forward guidance that signals a pause in the tightening cycle, mitigating the negative market impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate, not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in inflation, signals a labor market weakening that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in a potential recession.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL does not rise
failure_condition: Other leading indicators (e.g., yield curve, ISM PMI) do not confirm an imminent recession, negating the bearish signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production, if accompanied by a rise in consumer prices, signals an inflationary overheating that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in a hawkish Fed response.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 1% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL also rises
failure_condition: The Fed responds to the inflation spike with only a modest rate hike, indicating the market's initial reaction was an overreaction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales, not accompanied by a rise in consumer prices, signals a healthy demand-driven expansion that will produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in stronger corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 1% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL does not rise
failure_condition: The retail sales strength is subsequently revealed to be driven by unsustainable borrowing or inventory accumulation, rather than organic demand growth.
